# Arm structural joints: C1 tie-rod joints + M1 inline roll (generated by `python -m rnd.joints`)

C1: the pitch hub → pitch tube and the yaw flange → yaw tube joints were 6 × M3 into heat-set inserts in pull-out. Both
are now **tie-rod joints**: steel or aluminium threads only, the printed tube and hub clamped in compression between
metal parts (rnd/parts/shoulder.py HUB_TIE, rnd/parts/roll.py YAW_TIE). M1: the inline GIM8108-36 output boss, its rear
screws and its hard stops.

Loads at each joint interface come from the twin (rnd/twin.py, CAD masses) as the full wrench of everything outboard of
the interface: **pull-off** N (along the joint axis, outboard), **bending** M (the prying moment, perpendicular to the
axis), **torsion** T (about the axis, carried by the double-D / hex form fit, not by the tie).
- **Basket** (R2d): the rnd/basket.py targets with the D20 motors and 4.54 kg per hand; every collision-free IK solution
  is kept (an upper bound on the planner's pick), × 1.5 dynamic.
- **Hug** (R2c, rnd/payload_study.py case B): upper arm hanging, forearm horizontal, 4.54 kg 0.30 m out along the
  forearm, yaw 0/±45°, × 1.5 dynamic.
- **Bump**: 140 N at the grasp point (R17 transient contact limit) in ±X/±Y/±Z, arm hanging / forward / abducted /
  elbow 90°, plus the arm's weight. A fault/abuse load: checked against ultimate, the joint may gap.
- **Stall**: each of pitch, roll and elbow at its peak (D20 set, the worse one) driving the hand into a rigid block (the
  block force = stall torque / lever, in the joint's direction of motion), same poses. Fault load, as the bump.

Joint model (clamp()): a rigid metal end plate (crank/clamp ring, aluminium flange) on the printed contact annulus,
which is a compression-only elastic foundation (E 1.8 GPa over the printed stack length), with the bolts/tie as springs
holding the preload. It gives the moment at which the interface starts to gap, and the bolt force and peak printed
contact stress under each case. Criteria: service (basket, hug) no gap and contact ≤ 12 MPa; fault (bump, stall) bolt
≤ proof load, thread strip ≥ 1.5 × the bolt force, contact ≤ 40 MPa (PETG compressive yield ≈ 55–60 MPa, ESTIMATE;
compression closes the layers, so the across-layer 12 MPa does not apply).

Preload over life (Neon review 2026-11-27, finding 3 / assumption 1): the flat "× 0.75 for creep" is replaced by a
creep model (life_preload(): effective modulus, creep coefficient φ bounded from printed-PETG data, + embedding + a
cold day), and each C1 tie now has a DIN 6796 disc-spring stack in series so the printed stack is not the only spring.
The service rows are checked at the life preload (no gap), the contact stress at the fresh preload. M1 rows (inline
GIM8108-36): output dowels with load sharing, the metal rear clamp (plate + sleeves), the two-bearing roll support
(61806 + the motor's output bearing: reactions per load case from the twin, misalignment preload), the hard stops.

## Hardware

- **Pitch hub ↔ pitch tube** (rnd/parts/shoulder.py HUB_TIE): 4 × M4 class 10.9 studs (DIN 976-1, cut to 78.8 mm) on r 15.5 at 45° + k·90°, Loctite 270 into the Ti-6Al-4V balancer crank (tapped through 4 mm, stud end flush with its inboard face; was 7075-T6: its thread strip was 1.25× the stall bolt force with the chamfers counted), Ø4.5 holes through the tube wall (r 11–20) and the hub, M4 nuts (ISO 4032 class 8, Loctite 243) on a stack of 5 × DIN 6796-M4 conical spring washers (in series, alternating) on a 6061 clamp ring r 11–21 × 2 in a 11.7 mm recess of the detach face; 1.5 kN each (≈ 1.3 N·m, ESTIMATE). Assembly: tube into the inner wall → crank + studs from the inboard side → belt → outer wall → hub over the double-D and the studs → ring, spring stacks, nuts.
- **Yaw flange ↔ yaw tube** (rnd/parts/roll.py YAW_TIE): 6061-T6 flange (its hex spigot stays the torque path). 6 × M3 × 40 ISO 4762 class 12.9 go down from the tube's top end, heads on 3 × DIN 6796-M3 each, on a steel clamp ring r 8.5–16.8 × 2 in a Ø34 × 7.5 counterbore (heads 0.5 mm under the top), through Ø3.4 holes in the wall into M3 threads tapped at the hex corners (r 11) of the flange's spigot + plate (8.3 mm engaged, Loctite 243); 1.0 kN each (≈ 0.5 N·m). Tightened from above on the bench, before the yaw block goes onto the roll output.
- Disc springs: DIN 6796 spring steel (not A2 stainless), load to flat M3 1.32 kN / M4 3.77 kN (DIN 6796 table). Sources: McMaster-Carr "DIN 6796 lock washers", norelem 07000, Bossard BN 794 (part numbers to confirm at order).
- Not drawn (rnd/parts/arm.py, arm track): the upper bone ↔ yaw flange screws. With the flange in aluminium they should be M4 into tapped holes in the flange, heads on washers on the bone flange, not inserts.

## C1: preload over life

φ = 2.0 design / 1.0 nominal (ESTIMATE, bounded from printed-PETG creep data: Aerospace 2022 9(3) 124, PMC12349189; Findley t^n + 1–2 decades of 40–50 °C shift); PETG α 68e-6/K (datasheet range 60–70e-6, ESTIMATE) vs steel 11.5e-6, assembled at 20 °C, coldest service 10 °C; embedding 10 µm per printed interface (ESTIMATE: FDM layer peaks; VDI 2230 gives ≈ 2–3 µm per machined metal interface, used for the metal joints).

- **pitch hub ↔ tube:** 4 × M4 10.9 at 1.5 kN = 6.0 kN → 8.8 MPa on the printed contact annulus r 12.0–19.0; 5 × DIN 6796-M4 in series under each nut (0.46 mm of spring travel at the preload, flat at 3.77 kN). Per bolt: bolt 43, print 169 µm/kN (63.6 mm of PETG: 253 µm elastic, 506 µm of creep at φ 2). Life preload (φ 2, embedding, 10 °C day) **0.84 kN (56 %)**; φ 1: 1.04 kN; without the disc springs 0.46 kN (31 %). No gap under the worst service wrench (30.0 N·m, 0 N) needs ≥ 0.92 kN → 0.91×; bare 0.50× (gaps) ❌
- **yaw flange ↔ tube:** 6 × M3 12.9 at 1.0 kN = 6.0 kN → 9.5 MPa on the printed contact annulus r 14.1–20.0; 3 × DIN 6796-M3 in series under each head (0.53 mm of spring travel at the preload, flat at 1.32 kN). Per bolt: bolt 36, print 138 µm/kN (35.7 mm of PETG: 138 µm elastic, 277 µm of creep at φ 2). Life preload (φ 2, embedding, 10 °C day) **0.69 kN (69 %)**; φ 1: 0.80 kN; without the disc springs 0.30 kN (30 %). No gap under the worst service wrench (32.6 N·m, 101 N) needs ≥ 0.69 kN → 0.99×; bare 0.43× (gaps) ❌

Service rows (basket, hug) need no gap at the life preload and ≤ 12 MPa at the fresh preload; fault rows (bump, stall) need bolt ≤ proof, thread strip ≥ 1.5 × bolt, contact ≤ 40 MPa (worst of the fresh / life preload and the flat-spring stiffness).

## M1: inline GIM8108-36

| Item | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 output boss ↔ 7075 adapter (torque path) | dowels alone 164 N·m = 1.60× stall at a 240 MPa bearing allowable, equal sharing assumed | 103 N·m = 1.00× the 102.9 N·m stall, 2.9× the 35.1 N·m drive limit (dowels bonded into the adapter; dry: 65 N·m = 0.64×) | ❌ |
| M1 rear mount: 8 × M4 into the 3.5 mm housing threads | 8 × M4 × 18 + washer + picked shim through 13.9 mm of PETG at 0.5 kN (4 µm of bolt stretch; friction 38 N·m at × 0.75 creep) | metal clamp: M4 × 25 ISO 10642 10.9 (6) / ISO 4762 12.9 in the stop bushes (2) through a 3 mm 7075 rear plate and Ø6/4.3 steel sleeves onto the motor at 1.6 kN → 1.11 kN after embedding (no print in the stack); friction 56 N·m = 1.59× the drive limit; engagement 3.0 ± 0.49 (never bottoms in 3.5) | ❌ |
| M1 roll support: 61806 (rear) + the motor's output bearing | 61806 on a printed stub, located axially, 68 mm from the motor bearing: hyperstatic (review: binds or idles) | 61806 floats axially (± 0.3 mm on the stub) and is bonded into an oversize seat in situ; the misalignment preload is bounded by the printed support's radial stiffness: ≤ 800 N (worst) / 240 N (RSS). 61806 s0 2.2 service / 1.0 fault (need 1.5 / 1.0); the motor bearing needs ≥ 1412 N radial in service, 3125 N at a fault | ✅ |
| M1 roll hard stops (both ends) | Ø10 pins at r 43 'pressed 18.5 mm into the floor + cup ring': the cup ring is r 38–48, so the seat had 0 mm of wall to the driver bore and 0 mm outside (and the pins were not in the CAD); 30 MPa at stall in that seat (1.35× of 40) | steel stop bushes (Ø10 × 8 proud) on two of the 8 rear M4, clamped to the motor housing through the rear plate: at stall print 13.7 MPa, bush 415 MPa, plate 115 MPa, pad 15 MPa → 1.81× (worst of the six) | ✅ |

- **M1 output boss ↔ 7075 adapter (torque path):** bearing allowable 150 MPa (reverted from 240: cast A380-class σ_y ≈ 160 MPa with no bearing factor, ESTIMATE until the seller names the boss material; a steel or wrought 6061-T6 boss would justify ≈ 240). 3 × Ø4 × 4 mm on r 14.25: 2.40 kN each; dowel stiffness 41 kN/mm (Huth, Ø4 steel in 4 mm Al + 7 mm 7075); the first dowel takes k·δ before the others touch: δ 8 µm (H7/m6 spread, ISO 286) when the dowels are bonded (Loctite 638) into Ø4.1 adapter holes while seated in the motor (the adapter's hole positions drop out) → 93 N·m; dry in jig-bored holes δ ≈ 40 µm (± 0.02 true position each side, ESTIMATE) → 56 N·m (the review's ≈ 55 N·m); equal sharing 103 N·m. + 3 × M4 × 10 csk at 1.5 kN, μ 0.15, metal on metal (no creep): 10 N·m (strip of 2.65 mm effective M4 in the cast boss ≈ 3.9 kN). Dowel shear 242 N·m (ISO 8734). Criterion: stall is a fault, checked at a yield-level bearing allowable at ≥ 1.0× (as bolts ≤ proof); the 7075 adapter side is 7 mm deep
- **M1 rear mount: 8 × M4 into the 3.5 mm housing threads:** stack per screw: bolt 13 + sleeve 7 + plate 1 µm/kN, 5 metal interfaces × 2 µm embedding (VDI 2230, ESTIMATE) → 69 % left, no creep term (the printed floor + cup ring are sandwiched between the plate and the motor face, sleeves -0.05 mm vs the print: located, not clamped). Friction μ 0.15 steel/Al (ESTIMATE). Engagement 25 − 22 = 3.0 mm, worst ± 0.49 (screw length js15 ± 0.42, ISO 4759-1; plate ± 0.05, sleeve ± 0.02): 2.51–3.49 in 3.5 mm, so no shim picking; strip at the shortest (2.16 mm effective) 3.2 kN vs the worst bolt 2.16 kN (1.5×; motor bearing 2325 N × 40 mm → 94 N·m on the bolt circle, load factor 1). Stall reaction through the sleeves into the print: 2.7 MPa bearing (Ø6 × 19 mm, 8 sleeves)
- **M1 roll support: 61806 (rear) + the motor's output bearing:** reactions from the twin wrench of the roll output (the static roll stage taken off) on supports -31.5 / 37.5 mm (69 mm apart): service (basket, hug × 1.5) 61806 526 N, motor 612 N; fault (bump, stall) 1981 / 2325 N. Misalignment: the stub and the cup's driver pilot are one print (Ø75.2 pilot on the Ø75 driver, 0.1 radial) → static offset ≤ 0.25 worst / 0.15 RSS mm (pilot fit + print coaxiality 0.1 + motor 0.05, ESTIMATE); the rotating seat's own error (the clevis/arm print loop) is taken out by bonding the outer race (Loctite 660, 0.3 mm radial gap) with the arm bolted at mid-travel. Radial stiffness of the printed rear support 1.6–3.2 kN/mm (fea.md: stub 288 N → 0.13 mm, rear arm 525 N → 0.09 mm, in series; × 2 upper bound, ESTIMATE). The extra 61806 friction at 800 N is 18 mN·m (SKF μ 0.0015): it does not bind or blind the collision observer. **Deleting the 61806** (the review's option) needs the motor's output bearing to carry 117 N radial + 36.3 N·m tilting in service and 345 N + 137 N·m at a fault (about its own centre): only a crossed-roller or a preloaded pair with M0 ≥ 137 N·m qualifies. Seller question still open (output bearing type, C0, M0) — until then the 61806 stays
- **M1 roll hard stops (both ends):** F = τ / r: 836 N at 35.1 N·m, 2450 N at stall, contact 4 mm off the plate. The bushes sit on the screw circle (r 42) at -68.75° / 156.25° (REAR_ANG0 21.25°, rear arm half-width 28.21: contact at -16.5° / 104°). Load path: bush → plate (Ø10 × 3 fitted, 3.44 kN, 115 MPa vs 7075-T6 σ_y 435) → the 6 csk screws (cone seats) → the motor housing: the stall torque closes housing ↔ output in metal; the print sees only the bush's Ø7 × 19 mm tail as a foundation (rigid bush on the plate pivot, linear pressure: 13.7 MPa at stall, 4.7 at the limit). Bush 42CrMo4+QT (R_p0.2 ≥ 750, EN 10083-3): 415 MPa in the Ø7/4.3 tail at the plate, 137 MPa in the Ø10/7.2 head. Edge distances: plate ring r 35–48: 1 mm outside the Ø10 hole, load along the ring (end distance ≥ 3 d to the next screw); print: 0.9 mm from the tail to the driver pilot (load tangential). Wear strip 20 × 8 × 1.5 stainless bonded in each roll_arm_rear edge: 5.2 / 15.3 MPa on the print
